text:
alice: Quick question — trying to get the client to route to our VPC-only endpoint (PRIVATE_API_HOST) and still use the HTTP proxy for egress. When I set ENV API_HOST=https://private-api.internal and HTTP_PROXY=http://10.0.0.5:3128, streaming fails after a few chunks. Any gotchas?

matt: Repro'd. If the proxy terminates TLS you might be hitting chunked transfer + proxy buffering. Can you paste a short curl reproduction?

alice: Sure — here's minimal test:
```bash
curl -v --proxy http://10.0.0.5:3128 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://private-api.internal/v1/stream?model=gpt-..."
```
Response starts then stalls around 5s.

sana: Two quick checks: 1) Is the proxy doing CONNECT for TLS or rewriting host header? 2) Is the SDK using `Expect: 100-continue` or any connection pooling that keeps connection alive but stalled?

ryan: Also confirm TLS handshake target — if proxy is intercepting and presenting its cert, the SDK's hostname verification will fail unless you trust proxy CA or use mTLS. We had a similar flub last quarter.

alice: The proxy is doing CONNECT. Host header is the private host. No custom CA. We do use SDK streaming client in Node with `maxRetries: 2`. Could retries be interfering?

helen: Retries shouldn't affect a single persistent stream — they only restart idempotent requests after a failure. But if the SDK gets a connection reset and auto-reconnect is enabled, you might see partial stream then restart. What's the Node SDK version?

alice: 0.9.4

matt: Known bug in 0.9.x — connection pool handles proxy CONNECT but drops keepalive for streams. Patch in 0.9.5 fixes it. Workaround: set env REDWOOD_STREAM_TIMEOUT to a higher value and enable `reconnectOnDrop: true` on client options for now.

alice: Can you paste sample Node config?

matt: sure:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiHost: process.env.PRIVATE_API_HOST || 'https://private-api.internal',
  token: process.env.RW_TOKEN,
  stream: { reconnectOnDrop: true, maxReconnects: 3 },
  // longer server read timeout to tolerate proxy buffering spikes
  streamTimeoutMs: parseInt(process.env.REDWOOD_STREAM_TIMEOUT || '30000', 10)
});
```

sana: For Python users, similar workaround:
```py
client = RedwoodClient(
  api_host=os.getenv("PRIVATE_API_HOST"),
  token=os.getenv("RW_TOKEN"),
  stream_reconnect=True,
  stream_timeout=30
)
```

alice: Thanks — two follow-ups:
1) Is it safe to set apiHost to an internal-only domain with the hosted control plane? (we use dedicated infra)
2) How do we handle auth when the proxy mints a token? We currently forward `Authorization` header.

ryan: If you're on Dedicated/Private, control plane is separate. Setting apiHost to internal point is fine for client -> runtime, but make sure control plane callbacks (webhooks) use host reachable by the control plane or use private control plane mode. I'll DM infra.

helen: About auth: if proxy mints tokens (forwarding a different Authorization), that's opaque to Redwood. Best is to keep the original Bearer header for auditing. If proxy injects its own, validate the audit log and add `X-Original-Auth` header to preserve identity.

devex-bot: Reminder: File an infra ticket if this requires a new proxy CA in our per-tenant truststore. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/tickets

matt: For code review: @ryan @sana can you review the 0.9.5 patch that adds proxy keepalive fix? PR #4621. Low-risk change, needs QA on Node stream + proxy combos.

sana: On it, will test with our proxy lab tomorrow. Also will add a note in SDK readme about "private host + proxy" patterns.

alice: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll try upgrade to 0.9.5 and report back.

ryan: Also FYI — if you can't upgrade immediately, adding `Connection: close` header in curl made the proxy not buffer for me (but it's a perf hit).

alice: noted. tagging this as resolved for now. :tada:
